settings.question: Where can I find real persuasive writing examples written by kids?
settings.answer: Right here. Every piece in our library was written by a real Australian kid aged 5 to 13 and published in theINmag, our print magazine. They are genuine pieces, not invented worksheet examples. Browse the persuasive section free online and read them exactly as the kids wrote them.

settings.question: Can I use these as mentor texts in my classroom?
settings.answer: Yes, please do. Teachers use our pieces as mentor texts for planning, shared reading and independent reading, and our submission terms cover classroom use. Project them, print them, pull them apart with your class. They are sorted by purpose, persuasive, informative and entertaining, so you can match your unit.

settings.question: Are these like the annotated "work samples" on the Australian Curriculum site?
settings.answer: They are cousins. ACARA's samples show assessment against achievement standards, while ours are real pieces by Australian kids aged 5 to 13, published in a magazine kids actually read. That makes them mentor texts your class will enjoy, showing what real kids their age genuinely write.

settings.question: Do you have persuasive writing examples for Year 3 and Year 5?
settings.answer: Yes, and more land with every issue. Our writers are aged 5 to 13, so pieces span the primary years, including the NAPLAN ones. Because each was written by a real kid, they set believable targets for your students rather than polished adult models.

settings.question: Is it free, and how often is new writing added?
settings.answer: The whole library is free to read online, no login needed. The pieces come from theINmag, which publishes three issues a year, and we add fresh kid-written pieces from every issue. So there is always new persuasive, informative and entertaining writing to bring into your classroom.

settings.intro:
Every piece in this library is a real writing sample created by an Australian kid and published in theINmag. Persuasive texts, informative texts and stories, all at genuine kid level, which makes them rare: mentor texts your students can actually measure themselves against.

Use them in planning, put one on the board as a shared read, or hand them over as independent reading. Kids inspiring kids is the whole idea, and here is why we built this library. New samples land with every issue.
